main_body: Hip-roofed shrine hall: a large green tile roof over a cream plaster wall with red posts and a dark double door, on a grey stone base
top_band: Light green ridge band at rows 4-8 (L 168/138), then the tile slope at rows 10-41 (L 138 to 47) down to a light eave edge at rows 42-43, with a red beam below it
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large sloped surface seen from above, with a trapezoid silhouette, a lighter ridge cap, a light eave edge at rows 42-43 and the red beam at rows 44-46 casting a shadow on the wall. This reads like the Beodeul house references. The wall below is a vertical face with an inset dark door grid and posts. No receding isometric side faces appear. The roof slope and the wall are both clearly present, so the 3/4 contract holds.

style.evidence: The roof ramp has about 6 greens, and the median of 11 colours per tile matches house-h112. But the whole piece has only 32 distinct colours, against 66 and 185 for the references. 83% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% on the references, so the outline reads as a near-black sticker line. The roof is regular vertical tile stripes with no per-tile scallops or highlights. The cream wall is a large, mostly flat field with sparse speckles. It looks thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
